I'm working on making /v/thebiggestproblem look more like this page, and I want to know how to make the gray colored areas behind the links and the hot/new/etc bar to be either black or transparent. I don't know jack about CSS and have been cobbling together bits of code I've been finding, but I've turned up nothing for this.
How do I change the link background color?

Here's something to get you closer to what you might be looking for. You will have to toy with the colors to get exactly what you want.

I never did like Maddox's choice in color schemes. :P

#header-container {
 background-color: #000;
 border-color: #000;
}
.tabmenu li {
 margin: 0px 0px 0px 0px;
}
.tabmenu li.selected {
 background: none;
 background-color: #000;
 border: 1px solid #ff0;
 border-width: 1px 1px 1px;
}
.tabmenu li.selected a {
 background: none;
 background-color: #000;
 color: #ff0;
}

#container {
 background-color: #000;
}

.even {
 background-color: #000;
 border-bottom: 1px;
 border-bottom-color: #222;
}

.link a.author {
 color: #f80;
}

.side .spacer.spacersection {
 background-color: #000;
}
.sidecontentbox .content {
 background-color: #000;
}

.btn-whoaverse.contribute {
 background: -moz-linear-gradient(center top,#333,#131313 );
 background: -webkit-linear-gradient( top,#333,#131313 );
 border-color: #222;
 color: #ff0;
}

.tabmenu li.disabled a.contribute {
 background: -moz-linear-gradient(center top,#333,#131313 );
 background: -webkit-linear-gradient( top,#333,#131313 );
 border-color: #222;
 color: #f80;
}

.btn-sub {
 background: -moz-linear-gradient(center top,#333,#131313 );
 background: -webkit-linear-gradient( top,#333,#131313 );
 border-color: #444;
 color: #ff0;
}

.alert-h1 {
 color: #f80;
}
.alert-h2 {
 color: #f80
}
.side a {
 color: #ff0;
}
.side a:visited {
 color: #ff0;
}

.tagline .post_upvotes {
 color: #ff0;
}
.tagline .post_downvotes {
 color: #f80
}
.promoted {
 background: -moz-linear-gradient(center top,#333,#131313 );
 background: -webkit-linear-gradient( top,#333,#131313 );
 border-color: #222;
 color: #f80;
}
